extracted.intended_audience: readers of political theology and Christian doctrine (theologians, clergy, educated lay readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Normative guidance for correct interpretation of Scripture, proper form and meaning of church rites (consecration, baptism, Eucharist), and assessing claims about ecclesiastical vs civil power. Focuses on avoiding misinterpretation, superstition, and illicit claims of authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope-based interpretation of Scripture
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not the bare Words, but the Scope of the writer that giveth the true light, by which any writing is to bee interpreted; and they that insist upon single Texts, without considering the main Designe, can derive no thing from them cleerly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret Scripture according to the author's overall design and harmony with the whole Bible; avoid deriving doctrine from isolated texts. Examples: avoid 'casting atomes of Scripture' to support partisan aims; prefer plain senses agreeable to the whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid wresting Scripture to political ends
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest abuse of Scripture... is the wresting of it, to prove that the Kingdome of God... is the present Church, or multitude of Christian men now living.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reinterpret texts to make the present Church equivalent to Christ's Kingdom in order to claim temporal authority; historical and scriptural contexts (e.g., Israel under Moses, election of Saul) must be considered before inferring ecclesiastical rule over civil matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify four causes of spiritual darkness
rubrics_metrics.description: Four Causes: (1) abuse and putting out the light of the Scriptures; (2) introducing the daemonology of the Heathen Poets (fabulous doctrines concerning Daemons); (3) mixing with the Scripture diverse reliques of Religion and vain Philosophy of the Greeks; (4) mingling false or uncertain Traditions and fained History.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating doctrines or practices, check whether they arise from one or more of these corrupting sources rather than from clear scriptural teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consecration changes use not nature
rubrics_metrics.description: To Consecrate... is to Offer, Give, or Dedicate... thereby to change, not the thing Consecrated, but onely the use of it, from being Profane and common, to be Holy, and peculiar to Gods service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat consecration as a dedication/separation of use. Claims that consecration changes the underlying nature of an object (e.g., bread into a literal body) are either extraordinary works of God or abuses (conjuration); the absence of sensible change argues against literal transubstantiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject turning consecration into conjuration/incantation
rubrics_metrics.description: When by such words, the nature or qualitie of the thing it selfe, is pretended to be changed, it is not Consecration, but either an extraordinary worke of God, or a vaine and impious Conjuration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ritual language should not be treated as magical formulae that alter substances. Beware of rites that function as 'charms' producing no sensible effect but demanding belief in a change of nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceremonies, words and gestures must be decent and significant
rubrics_metrics.description: Those governors are obliged to such direction, as the nature of the action it selfe requireth; as that the ceremonies, words, and gestures, be both decent, and significant, or at least conformable to the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design rites to be rationally connected to their intended meaning (examples: Moses' anointing, Solomon's dedication) rather than arbitrary procession, exorcisms, spittle, or theatrical additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppose exorcisms and incantations in sacraments
rubrics_metrics.description: The like incantation, in stead of Consecration, is used also in the Sacrament of Baptisme... The Priest blows thrice in the Childs face, and sayes, 'Goe out of him unc clean Spirit'... These... are Charms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices that resemble conjurations (exorcistic formulas on water, oil, or infants, blowing in faces, repetitive conjurations) are improper additions and should be rejected as superstitious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid enchanted objects and charms in other rites
rubrics_metrics.description: In Marriage, Extreme Unction, Visitation of the Sick, Consecrating Churches... there is the use of Enchanted Oyle, and Water, with the abuse of the Crosse... as things of efficacy to drive away Phantasmes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on 'enchanted' sacramentals (conjured oil/water, formulaic blessings claimed to repel spirits) as evidencing true sanctity or efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate doctrines about the soul by whole Scripture
rubrics_metrics.description: The Soule in Scripture, signifieth alwaies, either the Life, or the Living Creature;... the Souls of the Faithfull, are not of their own Nature, but by Gods speciall Grace, to remaine in their bodies, from the Resurrection to all Eternity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret texts about immortality and the soul in light of the whole Bible—do not assume innate immortality of the soul as a natural property; immortality of the elect is a gracious gift tied to resurrection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read difficult texts in light of immediate context
rubrics_metrics.description: Explication of Mark 9.1: the words may relate to the Transfiguration and ought not be pressed to prove the Kingdom is already present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a passage appears to support a contentious doctrine (e.g., kingdom present at Resurrection), examine immediate narrative context (e.g., following verses, repeated accounts, related injunctions) before drawing doctrinal conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be suspicious of claims that centralize ecclesiastical authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If the present Church is Christs Kingdome, there ought to be some one Man, or Assembly, by whose mouth our Saviour... speaketh... This power Regal under Christ, being challenged, universally by that Pope... cometh to be so passionately disputed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question doctrines that assert a single human office (Pope, presbytery) as the sole representative of Christ with temporal authority; assess historical and scriptural bases for such centralization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question juridical elevation of canonical rules
rubrics_metrics.description: From the same mistaking... came in the distinction betweene the Civill and the Canon Laws... Which Canons, though they were but Canons... yet afterwards... became Rules Commanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat canonical rules skeptically when they are transformed from voluntary ecclesiastical precepts into civil laws; evaluate the original voluntary nature and historical evolution before accepting their civil authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use isolated scriptural examples to override civil obedience
rubrics_metrics.description: Whosoever therefore obeyeth his Christian Soveraign, is not thereby hindred, neither from beleeving, nor from obeying God... if a Christian King should... draw some false consequences... he shal be saved... much more shall he that teacheth them by his command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect civil sovereignty in ordinary cases; individual subjects should not presume to disobey lawful sovereigns on grounds of private interpretation unless clearly warranted and judged by appropriate ecclesiastical authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical-temporal reading of 'Kingdom of God' claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Whereas the Kingdome of God was first instituted by the Ministery of Moses... and ceased afterward... the Kingdome of God is not yet come, and wee are not now under any other Kings by Pact, but our Civill Soveraigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret 'Kingdom of God' claims with attention to historical development (Mosaic institution, election of Saul, promised future restoration) rather than treating them as a present political structure justifying clerical rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish devotionally-significant acts from magical efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The words, 'This is my Body,' are aequivalent to these, 'This signifies, or represents my Body;' and it is an ordinary figure of Speech: but to take it literally, is an abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor figurative/representative readings of sacramental words where literal readings imply invisible, senseless changes; do not conflate devotional symbolism with metaphysical transformation without clear scriptural warrant.
